summary: Trinity-area lookout on Bowerman Ridge, built in 1957 to watch the Trinity Dam site; listed as gone, with an old lookout site on a forest bike route.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; a Forest Service ride guide describes only an old lookout site.

access.note: Reached by Forest Service roads (35N24 and Bowerman Ridge Road, 36N35) on a published ride route; the sources do not say the site itself is open.

events.note: Completed early in 1957; construction had been announced in August 1956
Manned in May 1957 by J.B. Hill and his wife Eva

evidence.supports: 1956 announcement: lookout to cover Trinity project area under construction, Trinity National Forest name
evidence.quote: Construction of the lookout for the Trinity National Forest in the Weaverville district to cover the Trinity project area now under construction.

evidence.supports: temporary wooden structure, 40 feet high, on Bowerman Ridge
evidence.quote: Located on Bowerman Ridge, due East of Old Minerville, the lookout will be a temporary wooden structure, 40 feet high.

evidence.supports: $12,500, financed by Bureau of Reclamation, built by suppression crew at Minersville guard station
evidence.quote: the new $12,500 lookout, financed by the Bureau of Reclamation, is being built by the suppression crew at the Minersville guard station.
Located on the ridge above old Minersville, the new lookout was completed early this spring.

evidence.supports: Forest Service crews did the construction work
evidence.quote: The Bureau of Reclamation financed the construction with crews from the U.S.F.S. doing the work.

evidence.supports: manned in May 1957 by J.B. Hill and wife Eva
evidence.quote: was manned this week by J.B. Hill and his wife Eva

evidence.supports: bird's-eye view of the Trinity Project dam from the lookout
evidence.quote: From the lookout a 'birds-eye' view of the Trinity Project dam is possible.

evidence.supports: fires could be reported to suppression crews
evidence.quote: Early detection of any fire can be reported to the suppression crews.

evidence.supports: record listed as gone (Bowerman Ridge, Trinity, Tower, Gone)
ride route follows Bowerman Ridge Road
route runs downhill to an old lookout site
evidence.quote: straight on the main road downhill to an old lookout site

evidence.supports: old lookout site has an excellent view of the southwest Trinity Alps and Trinity Lake
evidence.quote: where you have an excellent view of the southwest portion

evidence.supports: guide issued by Weaverville Ranger Station, Shasta-Trinity National Forest
evidence.quote: Weaverville Ranger Station - Shasta-Trinity National Forest

evidence.supports: dam completed in early 1960s as part of Central Valley Project
evidence.quote: The dam was completed in the early 1960s as part of the federal Central Valley Project to provide irrigation water to the arid San Joaquin Valley

corrections.why: The 1956 notice used the older forest name; the Weaverville Ranger Station ride guide is issued by Shasta-Trinity National Forest

sources.title: Mountain bike routes, Weaverville Ranger Station (PDF)
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service, Shasta-Trinity National Forest

notes_for_editor: Gone status is from the FFLA California list only; no source gives the removal date or how it ended. The FS ride guide's old lookout site is on Bowerman Ridge Road but the guide does not name the lookout, so matching it to the 1957 structure is an inference. Height 40 ft is from the 1956 announcement (planned), not a measured built structure. Register NHLR US 394 CA 58 appears on the FFLA list but the record's registers field is empty and no NHLR page is cached; not checked. Staffing after 1957 unknown. Agency name is a proposed correction.
